transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what's been troubling you that brought you here today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, so I guess the main thing that pushed me to come in is... well, I process insurance claims for a living, and I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews. It's like I just have to move. Speaking of moving, my cousin just bought this huge RV. We were talking about it this weekend, and he’s planning to drive it all the way to Yellowstone. I’ve always wanted to go to Yellowstone, you know? The geysers and everything. I saw this documentary about supervolcanoes once, and it’s crazy to think what’s under there. But yeah, at work, I just can't seem to stay in my chair.
You mentioned that you get up from your workstation often, even when you know you should stay put. Do you feel restless or unable to sit still for extended periods?

Yeah, pretty much. Like, if we have trainings or those longer team meetings, I’m usually bouncing my leg or shifting around in my chair the whole time. Or clicking my pen. I actually have this really nice metal pen—it's one of those engraved ones my dad got me when I got this job. He was so proud I landed a desk job with benefits, you know? He worked construction his whole life, so he always wanted me in an office. His knees are completely shot now, he had to get surgery last year and the physical therapy was just a total nightmare for him. But um... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, even when I’m really trying to look focused in those meetings, I just can't stop clicking that pen or shifting around.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

No, not really. I don't think I'm a big worrier. My mom, though, she worries enough for both of us. She calls me like every morning just to make sure I set my alarm. Which is funny because I actually use my phone for my alarm, not a regular clock. I downloaded this new app that makes you solve a math problem before the ringing turns off. It's supposed to wake your brain up, but honestly, I usually just do the math half-asleep and go right back to bed. Math was never my strong suit anyway. I actually dropped calculus when I was in college because the professor just mumbled the whole time and I couldn't understand a word he said. He had this really thick mustache that covered his entire mouth, so you couldn't even try to read his lips. It was super distracting. But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Something about worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really sit around stressing about things.
Have you ever experienced times when you felt unusually upbeat, energetic, or so good that you didn't really need much sleep?

Um, unusually upbeat? No, I don't think so. I mean, I like sleep. A lot. I'm definitely not one of those people who can just run on three hours of sleep and a Red Bull. My roommate, though, he's insane like that. He works at this startup downtown, and he'll be up until 4 AM coding, and then he's up at 7 AM making a smoothie. He has one of those really loud blenders, like a Vitamix or something, and it sounds like a jet engine taking off in the kitchen. I keep telling him to put a towel under it to muffle the sound, but he never remembers. He's a good guy, but man, that blender... we actually found it at a thrift store for like twenty bucks, which is a total steal because those things are normally hundreds of dollars. But yeah, no, I definitely need my sleep. I don't ever get, like, super energized or anything like that.
Do you often feel uncomfortable staying seated for long periods, even when you know you should?

Wait, didn't we just talk about this? Yeah, with the meetings and the clicking pen and all that. I mean, yeah, I definitely have a hard time staying in my chair. Like I said, I'm always shifting around or getting up to grab water or whatever. Actually, speaking of water, the water cooler on our floor broke last week, and it was a total disaster. It started leaking everywhere right next to the copy machine, and the carpet got completely soaked. It smelled like wet dog for three days. The maintenance guy, Gary, he was so mad because he had just vacuumed that area. Gary's a funny guy, he always wears these crazy Hawaiian shirts on Fridays, even in the dead of winter. He said he gets them from some vintage shop near his house. But um... yeah, sorry. Like I said before, sitting still for a long time is definitely tough for me.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks, especially ones that require sustained attention, like paperwork or listening during meetings?

Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, my whole job is basically paperwork since I process insurance claims. But if I see a file come across my desk that needs, like, a really long written explanation, or if I have to check a bunch of dense policy language, I just... I'll put it off. I'll just sit there and do all the easier, quick tasks until I'm basically out of time for the day. 

Like, last week I had this one claim about a tree falling on a shed, and the policy language was so old, it was from like 1998. Which is crazy because that's the year my younger brother was born. We actually just celebrated his birthday. We went to this ridiculous arcade bar downtown, and they had the original Pac-Man machine—you know, the sit-down kind with the glass top? I used to play that exact game at Pizza Hut when I was a kid. Do you remember when Pizza Hut used to have those bumpy red plastic cups? Man, soda always tasted so much better out of those red cups for some reason. I think I drank like three Dr. Peppers that night and then couldn't sleep. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, focusing on paperwork. Yeah, I definitely avoid the complicated files until the very last second.
Do you find yourself often talking more than you intend to, or finishing other people's sentences because you feel impatient?

Um, talking too much or finishing sentences? No, I don't really think I do that. I mean, I'm pretty good at letting people finish what they're saying. My mom, though, she is terrible about that. You literally cannot get a full sentence out around her. She's always jumping in, assuming she knows what you're going to say. 

Actually, she did that just the other day when we were talking about my car. I drive this old Honda Civic, and the check engine light came on. I was trying to tell her that I thought it was the oxygen sensor, because I looked it up on YouTube. There's this one channel, I think it's called "ChrisFix" or something, and he's so good at explaining car stuff. He always uses soapy water to find leaks, which is such a smart trick. I actually tried it on my bike tire last summer when I ran over a piece of glass near the park. That park is really nice, they just put in a new dog run. I don't have a dog, but I like watching them run around. There was this one golden retriever that kept trying to catch a frisbee but kept missing it by like two feet. It was hilarious. 

But yeah, anyway, my mom just kept interrupting me to tell me I need to buy a new car, which I can't afford right now. So, no, I don't really interrupt people or talk too much. I think I'm a pretty good listener.
Do you often feel like you're 'on the go' or as if you're being driven by a motor inside you, making it hard to slow down or relax?

Driven by a motor? Um, no, not really. If anything, I feel like my motor is completely out of gas by the end of the day. I definitely don't have that crazy energy where I can't slow down or relax. 

Actually, speaking of motors, my buddy just bought this old aluminum fishing boat with a busted outboard motor that he's trying to fix up in his driveway. We actually took it out on the lake last weekend to test it out, and the thing completely died on us right in the middle of the water. We had to paddle all the way back to the dock with these tiny, cheap plastic emergency oars. It took like two hours, and my arms were so sore the next day I could barely lift my coffee mug at work. Which really sucked, because Mondays are always our absolute busiest day for processing claims. It's like everyone gets into weird accidents over the weekend and then Monday morning my inbox is just a total nightmare. I really don't understand why people do so much dangerous stuff on their days off anyway. Like dirt biking. Have you ever seen those videos of people doing backflips on dirt bikes? It looks absolutely terrifying. One wrong move and you're just... done. 

But, um... wait, sorry. You were asking if I feel like I'm always on the go? Yeah, no, definitely not. I'm usually just exhausted and want to crash on the couch.
